validatedTree: baseCommit plus the changes identified by sourceFileSha256 (documentation excluded)
scope: CORE-HARDENING structure foundation item 3 (API contract single source), first set: installations, runtime jobs, audit and groups; item 2's inconsistency 9

crates/miy/src/api_contract.rs (client and server) defines Installation, InstallationPage, AppDetail, RuntimeJob, RuntimeJobPage, AuditEntry, AuditPage and Group. The server answers through them; the CLI reads runtime jobs, the request-ID job lookup and app details through them

contracts/api-v1.schema.json is generated from the types (a Rust unit test fails when it is stale); packages/sdk/src/api.gen.ts is generated from the schema (node scripts/api-types.mjs --check fails when it is stale). The SDK re-exports the generated types and the platform's installation, audit and group types use them

Compatibility: responses only add fields. contracts/api-v1.published.json holds what published CLIs may read; scripts/check-api-compat.py fails on a removed type or field, a field no longer always sent, or a value that was not allowed before, unless listed as removable with a reason. Fields an older (0.7.0) server does not send are read with defaults
Item 9: the default, paged and runtime-management installation lists and the app detail use one SQL row (domain::INSTALLATION_ROW) and one conversion (domain::installation_view)
scripts/check-write-decisions.py (item 2, third step) also runs in the CLI foundation workflow's Linux server job
behaviorChanges: GET /api/v1/installations without a page query and GET /api/v1/runtime/installations now also return generation, lastOperation, appDisabled and canOpen (canOpen and appDisabled were in the management list only)
GET /api/v1/installations with a page query and GET /api/v1/apps/{app} now also return ui, health.errorCode, appDisabled, canOpen and acceptance.structured
Runtime job pages now also return installationId, like a single job

The CLI rejects a runtime job, job lookup or app detail response that does not match the contract (invalid_job_response, invalid_jobs_response, invalid_app_response); it still prints the server's JSON, including fields it does not know
